name: Improper Resource Shutdown or Release
principle: The product fails to release, close, unregister, or otherwise complete the lifecycle of a resource on a normal or exceptional path.
detection_signals: A resource is acquired and an error or early-return path skips its release or close operation
A callback, listener, lock, file, socket, or handle remains registered or held after its effective lifetime
Cleanup handles only the success path or releases an outer object while owned resources remain active
negative_signals: Every ownership-ending path reaches matching release, close, unregister, defer, finally, or RAII cleanup
Ownership transfer is explicit and the receiving owner performs the complete release
Failure cleanup is centralized and covers each resource that may have been acquired
false_defense_traps: Checking acquisition success but skipping cleanup after a later failure
Dropping a handle or setting it to null without releasing the underlying resource
Assuming process exit or garbage collection will promptly release a live service resource
verification_focus: For each acquired resource, is release or an explicit ownership transfer complete on normal, failure, and exceptional paths?
patch_principle: Use one cleanup path for all partially acquired resources
Release callbacks, locks, handles, and memory on every applicable exit path

minimal_examples.vuln: fd = open(path, flags); if (parse_error) return -1; close(fd);
minimal_examples.safe: fd = open(path, flags); if (parse_error) { close(fd); return -1; } close(fd);
